context: Philips Leadership Development Center Report for Dattatreya Vellal, 2020. Prepared by Rhys Connolly and Milind Murlindar Dixit (Zircon Management Consulting Ltd). Assesses leadership capability against Philips leadership and culture behaviors via development center activities, Swift Management Aptitude, Decision Styles and Strengths Insights questionnaires. Valid for up to two years. Contains executive summary, 8 leadership behavior assessments with strengths and development areas, and 3 key development objectives.
raw_text:
=== EXECUTIVE SUMMARY ===
A customer focused and data driven individual. Throughout the development center, demonstrated desire to add value for Philips customers. Data orientation enables well-informed and confident approach to challenges and opportunities. Highly accountable approach — proactively identifies areas to add greater value by challenging the status quo. Genuine desire to take personal responsibility and ownership for driving improvement and positive change. Significant strength in being articulate — effectively breaks down complexity for others and creates a safe and open space for conversations. Risk of overusing articulateness — approach to more senior stakeholders can trigger surprising responses. Could benefit from leveraging reflective approach to implement insights about self and others to influence interaction style with different stakeholders. Ability to break down complexity into simple steps can at times be a barrier to connecting with others on the bigger picture.

To further develop impact across Philips, could benefit from supporting others to recognize the 'why' behind specific change. Oftentimes has the numbers internally and draws valid conclusions, however others may not have sight of these. At risk of overusing focus on taking responsibility — can result in taking ownership for things that could be empowered to others. Seeking to better understand others' expectations and perceptions, and being more willing to have challenging conversations, could support in this area.

=== LEADERSHIP BEHAVIORS ===

1. CUSTOMERS FIRST
Strengths: Focus is clearly on improving the experience of Philips customers. Data-focused approach drives tangible impact on customers. Demonstrated during Board Presentation. During Customer Role Play remained patient and attentive to the customer's perspective, while taking personal ownership to ensure improvements are made.
Development: Segregating short and long-term plans and connecting on the greater purpose rather than immediate issues could help transition conversations to broader strategic ones. During Customer Role Play would have benefited from responding directly to challenging questions rather than moving on.

2. QUALITY AND INTEGRITY ALWAYS
Strengths: Profile displays as meticulous and genuine. Energized by ensuring work is delivered to highest quality and by operating in line with values. Demonstrated patience, fairness, and openness to other perspectives during customer role play, while remaining firm when discussing challenging topics. Desire and ability to identify issues and take personal ownership for driving improvements enables significant and positive impact. Role models appropriate behaviors, challenging others to do the same.
Development: Ensuring not to avoid the most challenging questions. Awareness that overuse of meticulous strength may be viewed as tendency towards perfectionism — could be a barrier to open communication.

3. TEAM UP TO WIN
Strengths: Ability to create a safe and open environment for challenging conversations demonstrated during role play activities — especially the employee role play. Recognized need to work cross-functionally to generate real impact during the case study.
Development: During customer role play, once scene was set and climate created for challenging topics, would have benefited from transitioning conversation onto topics which needed to be addressed. Approach to case study would have benefited from greater focus on breaking down organizational silos and creating a shared sense of purpose.

4. TAKE OWNERSHIP TO DELIVER FAST
Strengths: Clear and strong desire to take ownership for driving improvements. Demonstrated during interview and Customer Role Play — not only listened to issues presented but took responsibility for ensuring they were overcome. During case study took action-focused approach while upholding desire to learn from issues and challenges to ensure actions had sustained long-term impact.
Development: Desire to positively impact situations can result in approaching conversations with the context already held, without truly considering what the person on the other side is seeking to understand. During Customer Role Play could have benefited from seeking to understand the goals of the customer in the conversation. During case study, could have had greater impact by more explicitly linking plans to organizational strategy.

5. EAGER TO IMPROVE AND INSPIRE
Strengths: Demonstrates continuous improvement mindset, adopting a holistic perspective of what can be done to drive improvement. During case study communicated relentless focus on improving customer experience. As a highly articulate individual, able to effectively communicate complexity to others, supporting them in understanding both the 'how' and 'why' of driving continuous improvement.
Development: At risk of overusing articulateness when under pressure — can result in being viewed as overconfident in own perspective. Communicating at highest levels can be perceived as repetitive at times. Considering how to engage others with the improvements required could support in strengthening impact.

6. ASPIRATION
Strengths: Aspirational individual — persistent, enthusiastic, and relentless in pursuit of goals. During interview, focus on remaining constantly engaged and learning from challenges was especially clear. Approach to Board Presentation demonstrated focus on setting challenging goals and disrupting the status quo to achieve more positive outcomes.
Development: During board presentation, could have benefited from making goals more tangible — utilizing data focus to ensure they were measurable. Taking this approach while simultaneously supporting others to see the bigger picture could enable greater engagement and buy-in. Being aware of potential pressure put on others due to focus on delivering excellence could support in managing interactions and influencing more effectively.

7. EMOTIONAL & SOCIAL INTELLIGENCE
Strengths: Positive individual demonstrating calmness and resilience under pressure. Willing to challenge others while remaining confident in own perspective, also demonstrating patience to listen to others during Customer Role Play. Keen awareness of others around — what motivates them, where their focus lies, and how that may misalign with own priorities.
Development: To maximize impact, could benefit from considering how to leverage knowledge gathered about others to influence interaction style and ensure positive impact. Recognized at times as a threat by others — transitioning this into being seen as someone who can support and be leveraged to drive positive change could enable greater impact.

8. BUILDING PARTNERSHIPS
Strengths: Effective in removing barriers to communication. During interview demonstrated desire to build common skills, perspective, and language to enable more successful collaboration. During Board Presentation, focus on highlighting how to build partnerships with external parties to drive improvements was a real area of success.
Development: To maximize impact in Board Presentation, could have benefited from considering how to engage with audience. Placing greater emphasis on articulating the bigger picture, and illustrating a journey connecting on values, purpose, and behaviors, could support in gaining greater engagement.

9. DRIVING INNOVATION
Strengths: Real desire to challenge the status quo. Generates and provides support to novel ideas while simultaneously collecting data that can enable getting support from others. Highly appreciative of new ideas — underpinned by constant focus on continual improvement and building upon the work of each other.
Development: Articulated innovation approach during interview, but was not evident during response to case study. Would have benefited from highlighting how to remove barriers to creativity and why change is important for enabling long-term success of the business.

10. BUSINESS ACUMEN
Strengths: Ability to draw trends from data demonstrated in approach to case study — made good conclusions from customer data and looked at revenue models from other countries. Remained focused on need to stay ahead of competition through disruption and to increase operating profits.
Development: Based on strong understanding of numbers and ability to identify trends in data, could have strengthened approach during presentation by using numbers with more directness and clarity. Connecting audience to wider more holistic vision would also have been beneficial.

=== KEY DEVELOPMENT OBJECTIVES ===
1. Consider what can be done to formulate and articulate a story or game plan which connects the big picture with more granular actions for everyone to understand for themselves. Actionable conclusions to conversations, with specifics marked and agreed upon by relevant parties, will allow driving change with greater conviction.

2. Reflect on how to approach difficult conversations by challenging others with data, without being perceived as judgmental or aggressive. Enabling others to understand the position being approached from, and the value that should be placed on the data, could be more effectively balanced with allowing those on the other side to share their perspective and be genuinely heard.

3. Being aware of the risks of overusing the articulate strength, and utilizing approaches to enable controlling this, could enable further developing impact with audiences. Allowing others the space to bring in their own perspective and details, while reacting to details in a concise manner, could enable retaining the involvement of others in discussions.
